title: Exit monitor silently never starts when the first price quote fails, so the position has no stop-loss, trailing stop or 30-minute exit until a restart

evidence.note: startExitMonitor: entryPrice = await queryPrice(...); if null -> ctx.log.error("Cannot query initial price, exit monitor not started") and return; no interval, no exit_state row, no retry, no Telegram alert
queryPrice returns null on any error (RPC error, revert, unsupported dex/feeTier combination), so one transient RPC failure right after the buy is enough
the exit_state row is written only after the quote succeeds, so the failed start leaves nothing persisted for the position
sibling: resumeExitMonitor with no exit_state row (exactly the state a failed start leaves) queries the price once more and returns the same way on null ("Cannot query price for resume, skipping")
armPositionMonitoring awaits startExitMonitor, which resolves normally on this path, so the caller cannot tell the monitor was not armed; anti-rug registration then still runs (:430-439)
V3 snipe path: same call, same silent return
codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): One initial quote failure leaves a purchased position without monitoring

sibling_sites_checked: All three monitor entry points: startExitMonitor (:1857-1946, returns on null at :1870-1873), resumeExitMonitor no-row branch (:1978-1984, same), resumeExitMonitor with a row (:1968-1977, no quote needed, starts). Callers at the base SHA: bot.ts:422 (armPositionMonitoring, V2 snipe and deliberate buy), bot.ts:1483 (V3 snipe), bot.ts:1948/:1955 (restart resume), exitEngine.ts:731 (re-arm after a failed exit; has a row, so it starts). The parseEther(buyAmountNative) at :1866 throws instead of returning for an invalid amount, which rejects armPositionMonitoring before the anti-rug registration (BUY slice, AUD-BUY-002 family).
severity_rationale: S1, equal to the research suggestion. Proven by the code: on a null first quote the function returns with no timer, no persisted state, no alert and no retry. The plausible condition is a single RPC error or quoter revert in the seconds after a buy (busy launch block). Anti-rug registration still runs, so the position is not fully unprotected, and a restart re-tries once; that bounds it below S0. Until then there is no stop-loss, trailing stop, partial take-profit or 30-minute urgency exit.
recommendation: Never return without an armed monitor: retry the first quote with backoff, or persist exit_state with an unknown entry price and keep the interval armed so it baselines on the first good quote; alert the operator on any start failure. Decide the policy on card EXIT-01 (Phase 24).
